S9.01.note: The code searches models only; the Expected line also names files, projects and skills, which this picker does not list.
steps: Sign in and open a new chat.
Tap the model button at the bottom of the message box (its accessibility label starts with "Model:").
In the sheet, tap the search field that says "Search models…" and type part of a model name.
Check that the list narrows to matching models only. Note: this picker lists models; files, projects and skills are not in it (files are searched in Library > "Search library").
S9.01.where: Chat > Model button at the bottom of the message box > Search models…

S9.02.note: Models that are locked for the account show a lock reason in the row, such as upgrade or sign-in needed.
steps: Sign in and open a new chat.
Tap the model button at the bottom of the message box.
In the sheet, tap a different model row (rows show "selected" for the current one).
Send a message and check the model shown on the button or the reply matches the model you picked.
S9.02.where: Chat > Model button at the bottom of the message box > model list

S9.04.needs: a connector with two or more linked accounts
S9.04.note: Searched apps/mobile for account selection in connector code. Settings > Connectors > a connector shows an "Account" row that lists linked accounts (ConnectorAccountSummary.tsx), but I found no control to choose which account a task or chat uses.

S9.05.needs: a cloud account in a team workspace
steps: Sign in with a cloud account that belongs to a team workspace.
Tap Settings, then the "Workspace" row.
Read the list: "Personal" and each team workspace name are shown, with a check mark on the active one.
Tap a row that is not checked; the screen switches workspace and the check mark moves to it.

labels.text: Choose the project context for this chat.

S9.06.needs: a Cloud account with at least one project
S9.06.note: The code also reaches the project picker from Add to chat; that menu label was not confirmed.
steps: Sign in and open a new chat.
Tap the project bar that says "No project" (its accessibility label is "Select a project for this chat").
In the picker, read the line "Choose the project context for this chat." and tap one of your projects.
Check the bar now shows the project name (accessibility label "Active project: ...").
S9.06.where: Chat > project bar above the message box > No project > pick a project

S9.10.needs: a Cloud account; an action that asks for approval
S9.10.note: No picker for API keys or site automation scope was found in the files read; this covers tool approvals only.
steps: Open Settings and tap "Capabilities", then the "Action approvals" row.
Read the three choices: "Ask before every action", "Run read-only actions without asking", "Skip approvals".
In a Cloud chat, ask the assistant to do an action that needs approval.
In the approval card, compare the choices "Allow once", "Allow for this chat", "Always allow" and "Deny" with Expected (once versus always).
S9.10.where: Settings > Capabilities > Action approvals (scope of tool approvals); the approval card in chat shows "Allow once", "Allow for this chat" and "Always allow"

S9.12.needs: a plan that includes Scheduled tasks
S9.12.note: The code offers only Once, Daily, Weekly and Monthly; no custom rule option was found, unlike the Expected line.
steps: Open the menu and tap "AGI Work", then "Scheduled tasks".
Tap "Create schedule".
Open the repeat choice and pick "Once", "Daily", "Weekly" or "Monthly".
Save, then check the task's list entry shows the chosen cadence.
S9.12.where: AGI Work > Scheduled tasks > Create schedule

steps: Open the menu (drawer) and tap "Library".
Read the chips "All", "Images", "Videos", "Documents", "Uploads", "Generated files", "Artifacts" and tap one to filter.
Tap the search bar that says "Search library" and type a name.
Tap a file to open it, then compare with Expected.

S9.15.needs: a Cloud or Local chat that returns a table
S9.15.note: The sort logic is in apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/MessageContentRenderer.tsx (headers are buttons with a sorted state); the header text itself is model output, so no fixed visible label was found.
steps: Ask the assistant for a table, for example a comparison of three items.
Look for the table in the answer and scroll it sideways if it is wide.
Tap a column header once; rows should reorder by that column.
Tap it again to reverse the order and compare with Expected.
S9.15.where: Chat > an answer that contains a table > tap a column header

S9.16.needs: none (a few saved files, artifacts or projects help)
S9.16.note: The grid uses a fixed test id "library-grid" in the code; the visible grid columns depend on screen width.
steps: Open the menu and tap "Library".
Check the items appear as cards in a grid.
Tap a card to open it.
Compare the card layout and opening with Expected.
S9.16.where: Menu > Library (cards shown in the grid)

S9.17.note: The code opens the library with an image id; the larger viewer itself was not traced.
steps: Open the menu and tap "Images".
Check the images show as a gallery of thumbnails.
Tap one image to open it in a larger view.
Compare the larger view with Expected.
S9.17.where: Menu > Images (or Menu > Library > Images chip)

S9.19.needs: a Cloud account; a request that runs tools
S9.19.note: Step order and per-step duration display were not traced in full.
steps: Send a Cloud request that uses tools (for example one that searches or runs an action).
When the reply is done, find the line that starts with "Worked for" and its elapsed time.
Expand the activity to list the steps in order and check each step's state (for example Paused, Failed, Stopped wording).
S9.19.where: Chat > a request that runs tools > the "Worked for" line under the reply

S9.20.needs: a Cloud account (the row shows "Cloud mode required" in Local mode)
S9.20.note: The newest-first ordering was not confirmed in the code read.
steps: Sign in with a cloud account and open Settings.
Tap "Security and login".
Find the section titled "Recent security activity".
Read the rows and check they are newest first, or that the row says "No activity recorded yet" when empty.
S9.20.where: Settings > Security and login > Recent security activity

S9.22.needs: none (Remote Control may be hidden in some builds)
S9.22.note: The walkthrough shows dots (StepDots); a text counter such as "Step 2 of 4" was not found.
steps: Open Settings and tap "Connections".
Open the companion screen from the remote control screen.
Tap "Show companion walkthrough".
Tap "Next step" to move forward and check the dots and the current step against Expected; "Finish walkthrough" appears on the last step.
S9.22.where: Settings > Connections > remote control screen > Show companion walkthrough

S9.23.note: No step counter text was found; saving of choices at the end was not traced.
steps: Install or reset to a fresh state and open the app.
Enter your name in the field labelled "Your name" and tap "Continue".
Choose a model and tap "Continue" or "Download model".
Look for "Sign in to use Cloud", then check that your choices were kept when the setup finishes.
S9.23.where: First launch > onboarding (name, model, Cloud sign-in)

S9.26.needs: an artifact with at least two versions
steps: Open an artifact from a chat that has several saved versions.
Tap the version control that reads "Version N of M".
In the history sheet, read each version and tap "Restore version" for the one you want.
Use "Previous version" and "Next version" to step through; compare with Expected.
S9.26.where: Chat > open an artifact full screen > the "Version" control (shows Version N of M)

S9.27.needs: a Cloud Code session with changed files
S9.27.note: The diff counts (file and line counts ending in "changed.") are in apps/mobile/src/features/companion/components/CodeSessionView.tsx, but I did not confirm the menu path that opens a session or the on-screen diff view.

S9.28.needs: a Cloud account with web search enabled
S9.28.note: The excerpt shown per source was not confirmed in the code read.
steps: Ask a question that uses web search so the answer has sources.
Tap the line that says "View 3 sources" (count varies) or "Sources so far" while streaming.
Read each source's title and origin, then tap one to open it.
Compare with Expected; the excerpt display was not traced.
S9.28.where: Chat > an answer with sources > "View N sources"

S9.29.note: The meter's assistive-tech values were not confirmed; the info control has an accessibility label.
steps: Sign in with a Cloud account and open Settings.
Tap "Usage".
Read the "Plan usage" section: each meter shows its label and a reset line below the bar.
Tap the info control labelled "About usage limits" and compare the reset time with Expected.

S9.31.needs: none (some rows need a Cloud account)
steps: Open Settings and tap "Capabilities".
Read the header "What AGI can use" and the rows (for example "Action approvals", "Web search", "Image generation").
Each row shows its state as a value on the right.
Tap "Action approvals" to see the approval choices, then compare with Expected.

S9.32.needs: a Cloud account; a tool action that needs approval
S9.32.note: Which actions ask depends on the policy and the tool, so the card may not appear for every action.
steps: Set Settings > Capabilities > Action approvals to "Ask before every action".
In a Cloud chat, ask the assistant to do an action that needs approval (for example a write or send action).
Read the approval card: it names the action and shows the choices.
Tap "Allow once" or "Deny" and check the run continues or stops, as Expected says.
S9.32.where: Chat (Cloud) > an action that needs approval > approval card with "Allow once", "Allow for this chat", "Always allow", "Deny"

S9.33.needs: a Cloud account; at least one connector
S9.33.note: The code maps states to connected, needs reauthorization and not responding; a visible "Expired" word was not found.
steps: Sign in with a Cloud account and open Settings.
Tap "Connectors".
Read each connector card: the "Connected" filter and the connected state shown on the card.
Open a connector and tap "Disconnect" (a confirmation asks first), then compare with Expected.

S9.34.needs: a Cloud or Local chat with a model that lacks a feature
S9.34.note: Searched apps/mobile/src/features/chat and apps/mobile/src/features/model-picker for "not support", "doesn't support", "can't send" and similar; ChatInput.tsx near line 880 is attachment handling, and no visible capability-warning notice was found.

S9.35.needs: a Cloud account; a running task; Remote Control may be hidden in some builds
S9.35.note: The progress bar is in apps/mobile/src/features/companion/components/AgentDashboard.tsx; the path from the task list to the agent screen goes through the companion screen, and the exact entry label was not confirmed.
steps: Start a long task in Cloud mode so it runs in the background.
Open the task from the task list and check the card shows its progress bar and current state.
Watch the card update while the task runs, then tap "Expand tool call log" to see the latest actions.
Compare with Expected (steps done, latest action).
S9.35.where: Remote control (AGI Work > Tasks > open a running task) > agent detail

S9.36.needs: a Cloud or Local chat that returns an interactive card
S9.36.note: Feedback from the choice into the conversation was not traced in full.
steps: Ask the assistant for a place, for example "show me a map of a city" or a day plan.
Find the map card in the answer and tap its action buttons.
Check the map shows the place with its overlay labels (route pill, attribution).
Tap a choice or action and see whether the answer or conversation updates, as Expected says.
S9.36.where: Chat > ask for a place or an itinerary > the map card in the answer

S9.37.needs: a signed-in account; at least one notification (an unread one shows the unread style); the cloud chat feature must be on, otherwise the screen shows nothing
S9.37.note: The unread-count button in the header (DrawerButton.tsx) opens the same inbox only on wide layouts; on phone the search route is the path found in code, and the Mark all as read button is icon only.
steps: Sign in and open the Chats screen.
Tap the search icon in the header (it has no visible text; the code labels it 'search').
Type Notifications (or inbox) in the Search box and tap Notifications under Go to.
Look at the title Notifications and the line under it: 'N unread notifications' or 'All caught up'. Unread rows show a bold title and a small dot, and their screen-reader label starts with 'Unread,'.
Tap an unread row to open it, or tap Mark read on it, then check that the row turns to the read style and the count goes down.
Check that the newest item is at the top.
S9.37.where: Chats > search icon in the header > type Notifications > under Go to, tap Notifications

S9.38.note: Not built on mobile, as the plan's ledger says (D-2026-09-28-27). I searched apps/mobile for keyboard handlers (keyCommand, useKeyCommands, onKeyPress, hardwareKey, keydown, shortcut) and found only Android launcher shortcuts in native/android/withAGIShortcuts.cjs, which are not an in-app palette. The Search screen (app/(app)/search.tsx) has no keyboard shortcut and no Enter-to-run.
